title: Brief gap-junction blockade persistently alters bioelectric state after drug washout

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Brief gap-junction blockade persistently alters bioelectric state after drug washout

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In G. dorotocephala, the long-lasting alteration of bioelectric patterning after brief octanol exposure is not caused by residual octanol (which leaves tissues within 24 h) but is initiated by octanol's disruption of gap junction communication, which alters bioelectric network topology and results in a persistent perturbation of bioelectric state.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.4. Bioelectric State of Tissues and Its Stable Alteration in Species-Specific Shape Change

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Although these long-lasting alterations in bioelectrical patterning are not directly caused by octanol remaining within the body of the worm (since 8-OH is known to depart planarian tissues within 24 h [20]), they are initiated by the octanol-mediated disruption of GJC, which alters bioelectric network topology, and results in persistent perturbation of bioelectric state.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “3. Discussion › 3.4. Bioelectric State of Tissues and Its Stable Alteration in Species-Specific Shape Change”. Scope: G. dorotocephala somatic tissues after transient octanol exposure

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public measurements support persistence after the expected washout period, but they do not directly establish the claimed causal chain from gap-junction topology to stable voltage state. Existing data therefore resolve only part of the mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Combine measured octanol clearance with longitudinal voltage imaging and direct gap-junction connectivity assays after washout. Persistent altered voltage after drug disappearance supports state persistence, while restored connectivity would test whether topology itself remains altered.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Alternative stable biochemical changes are not excluded.

The octanol-clearance result comes from prior work.

Persistent DiBAC patterns do not directly measure network topology.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Separating residual drug from a persistent change in coupling requires chemical, conductance, and voltage measurements on the same animals. This paper cites a washout interval from earlier work and shows later voltage images. Those paired measurements are not public, so the mechanism remains untested with existing data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure octanol remaining in tissue after washout, gap-junction conductance, and the later voltage pattern in the same animals. Persistent voltage change after the drug is gone, tracking a changed coupling topology, would support the memory claim; residual drug or unchanged coupling would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Tissue octanol and direct gap-junction conductance were not measured in this cohort.

A later voltage change is compatible with several persistent injuries besides a rewritten network topology.
